newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ramos given clean bill of health for 10-day trip.
newsitem.headline: Ramos given clean bill of health for 10-day trip.

text.p: Doctors gave Philippine President Fidel Ramos a clean bill of health on Friday after a two-hour check-up, just days before he is scheduled to begin a trip to South Asia and the Middle East.
The check-up was to determine his state of health before the 10-day tour, which starts on Sunday.
"We have given him a clean bill of health," Raul Fores, the president's doctor told Reuters.
Ramos invited reporters to see how he did on the treadmill and other exercises on Friday to clear doubts about his health.

The president, a workaholic who prides himself on his physical fitness, underwent major surgery last December to remove a cholestrol blockage in his neck which could have been life-threatening if not removed.
"The main defect was I have to change the left lens of my eye glasses," Ramos said on Friday, adding that he passed his exercises "all with flying colours".
Fores said the president's blood pressure was 130/80. "That's perfect," he said.
A team of doctors will accompany Ramos during his overseas trip, he said.
Since his operation in December, there has been widespread concern in the country over his health and many people have asked him to slow down.
On Friday, the Philippine Star newspaper criticised Ramos for exerting himself at the 11th anniversary celebrations of the 1986 Edsa People Power movement.
During Tuesday's celebrations Ramos repeated a jump he did 11 years ago after learning that then ruler president Ferdinand Marcos had fled the country.
"Such an exertion might have proved costly to the nation," the Star's publisher Max Soliven said in his column.
